name: Antigua and Barbuda
summary: Antigua and Barbuda does not tax individuals' income (personal income tax was abolished in 2016), and has no capital gains, dividend, inheritance, estate or wealth tax. Self-employment and unincorporated business income bears unincorporated business tax (0-25%). Real estate transfers are costly: 7.5% seller and 2.5% buyer stamp duty, a 5% alien landholding licence for non-resident buyers and 5% tax on appreciation for non-resident sellers. Citizenship by investment from USD 230,000 (National Development Fund) or USD 300,000 real estate.

regimes.name: Ordinary residence
regimes.description: No personal income tax; unincorporated business tax on self-employment/business income only.
regimes.eligibility: Any lawful resident; non-citizens need a residence permit or citizenship.

capital_gains.summary: No capital gains tax on securities or business interests. Land sales by non-residents/non-citizens bear a 5% tax on the appreciation.
capital_gains.rate_basis: No CGT (Deloitte 2026). real_estate_local is null: the 5% appreciation tax applies to non-resident sellers (Deloitte) or non-citizens (IRD name); whether a resident non-citizen pays it is unclear.

open_questions: Rate base and scope of the land value appreciation tax for resident non-citizens.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Stamp duty on sale of real property: 7.5% seller and 2.5% purchaser on value. Non-resident purchasers also need an Alien Landholding Licence costing 5% of value; non-resident sellers pay 5% stamp tax on the appreciation in value (the IRD lists a 'Non-Citizen Land Appreciation Tax' paid at the time of sale). Share sales: 5% seller, 2.5% buyer. Undeveloped land owned by non-residents: annual 10-20% tax on land value.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Trading carried on as an unincorporated business is subject to unincorporated business tax at 0-25% on worldwide income for residents.

dividends.summary: No tax on dividends received by individuals; no withholding tax on dividends.

sources.title: Deloitte International Tax: Antigua and Barbuda Highlights 2026 (updated January 2026)

dividends.withholding_outbound: 0% on dividends to residents and non-residents; 25% on interest and royalties to non-residents.
dividends.treaty_network: Treaties with Switzerland, UAE, UK and the CARICOM multilateral treaty; BEPS MLI signed 18 June 2025. No US treaty.

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Property tax 0.2%-0.5% of market value by use; non-resident undeveloped land tax 10%-20% of land value.

sources.title: Deloitte International Tax: Antigua and Barbuda Highlights 2026 (updated January 2026)

inheritance.summary: No inheritance or estate tax; gifts may be subject to stamp tax.
inheritance.gift_tax: No gift tax, but gifts of property may be subject to stamp tax (Deloitte 2026); rate for gifts not verified.

sources.title: Deloitte International Tax: Antigua and Barbuda Highlights 2026 (updated January 2026)

open_questions: Stamp duty and fees on land passing on death and on gifts of land to children.

residency.tax_residency_test: No personal income tax; residence matters only for unincorporated business tax and property-transfer rules (non-resident surcharges).

routes.name: Citizenship by investment: National Development Fund
routes.requirements: USD 230,000 one-time contribution per application, any family size. Processing fee USD 10,000 single, USD 20,000 family of up to 4, plus USD 10,000 per additional dependant. Due diligence USD 8,500 main applicant, USD 5,000 spouse, USD 2,000 per child 12-17, USD 4,000 per dependant 18+.

routes.name: Citizenship by investment: approved real estate
routes.requirements: Approved property of at least USD 300,000, not resold for 5 years; same processing and due diligence fees.

corporate.summary: Corporate income tax 25% (22.5% for certain banks); no participation exemption; foreign tax credits only for Commonwealth jurisdictions with reciprocal relief or by treaty. No Pillar Two commitment. No WHT on dividends.

sources.title: Deloitte International Tax: Antigua and Barbuda Highlights 2026 (updated January 2026)

us_citizen_notes: US citizens stay subject to US federal tax on worldwide income, gains and estate; with no local income tax there is no local tax to credit, so the US layer applies in full. No US-Antigua income tax treaty.
open_questions: CBI residence requirement (reported as 5 days in 5 years) and any 2025-2026 price or due-diligence changes, including the Eastern Caribbean regional CBI regulator, not verified on an official page.

intl_school_annual_fee.description: Island Academy International School (IB), grades 12-13 (IB Diploma) annual tuition 2026-27; grades 10-11: XCD 22,500. Plus a one-time IB two-year resource fee of XCD 900 and IB exam entries billed in grade 13.

prime_rent_monthly.description: Median of the seven priced 4-5 bedroom homes among Chestertons Antigua's long-term rentals on 15 Oct 2026: Villa Ensueno, Crosbies (5 bed) USD 10,000; The Butterfly House, Cedar Valley USD 5,500; Villa Barbarella, Crosbies USD 4,200; Tamarind House, Hodges Bay USD 4,000; Marble Hill House USD 3,000; Creek House, St John's USD 3,000; Villa De Soleil, Mt Pleasant USD 2,800 (4 bed unless stated; one further 5-bed, Villa Capri at Galley Bay Heights, price on application). Listings are undated and utilities are extra. Lush Locations (Villa Management Ltd, Jolly Harbour) long-term list the same day had five priced 4-5 bed homes (USD 1,600-10,000), also with a median of USD 4,000.
